title: How Social Learning Keeps Orangutans Fed - Nautilus
gist: A study in Science draws on 12 years of observing wild Sumatran orangutans at Suaq Balimbing. It shows that young orangutans learn a diet of about 250 food types by watching their mothers and then trying themselves, during a parenting period of about eight years.

insights.claim: A Science study analyzed 12 years of observation data on wild Sumatran orangutans (Pongo abelii) at the Suaq Balimbing research area in Sumatra, Indonesia.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Long-run field datasets support research on how culture and learning evolve, but the investment relevance is low.
insights.quote: analyzed observation data collected over 12 years at the Suaq Balimbing research area in Sumatra, Indonesia

insights.claim: Wild orangutans eat about 250 food types, and many need specific techniques to obtain, such as using sticks to pull ants out of trees.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Complex learned foraging makes the species vulnerable when habitat loss breaks up its social transmission of skills.
insights.quote: encompassing about 250 food types in the wild
insights.locator: Diet is central to orangutan life

insights.claim: Young orangutans learn what to eat and how to get it from their mothers over a parenting period of about eight years, first by watching and then by trying.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: A long dependency period means slow population recovery, which is relevant to conservation and to deforestation for palm oil in peat forests.
insights.quote: During the lengthy parenting period of eight years, immature orangutans learn what and how to eat from their mothers
insights.locator: Diet is central to orangutan life
